methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Roanoke College launches WorkAI Lab to prepare leaders for new era of technology - Roanoke College
signals.signal_reading: A WorkAI Lab at Roanoke College signals intentional capability-building in a non-metro region, creating potential for distributed deep learning if it develops peer networks beyond campus boundaries rather than remaining an isolated institutional initiative.

signals.title: Norfolk native brings free AI workshops to Hampton Roads to close the technology gap - WTKR
signals.signal_reading: Free community AI workshops led by a Norfolk native directly target distribution and accessibility, potentially seeding peer-to-peer learning networks that could enable deep adoption outside traditional tech hubs if sustained beyond initial sessions.

signals.title: TAYLOR: AI data centers increase Virginia’s urban-rural divide - The Cavalier Daily
signals.signal_reading: Explicit acknowledgment that data center concentration in NoVA deepens urban-rural divides signals infrastructure investment flowing to already-capable regions while economic benefits remain geographically locked, reinforcing rather than bridging the capability gap.

signals.title: AI pressure grows on Richmond's young workforce - Axios
signals.signal_reading: AI pressure on Richmond's young workforce suggests rapid platform-driven adoption creating displacement anxiety without corresponding deep skill development, pointing toward shallow engagement where workers adapt to AI tools rather than building AI capability.

signals.title: Tech Briefs: Virginia Tech adds an artificial intelligence minor to its curriculum - Cardinal News
signals.signal_reading: Virginia Tech's AI minor concentrates advanced curriculum development at an existing research institution, potentially deepening capability in the New River Valley hub while raising questions about whether this knowledge diffuses to community colleges and regional campuses serving underserved areas.
